name: hero-with-opening
purpose: The opening band of a product page followed straight by its arguments: a large centered title band with the page `h1`, overline, sentence and up to two actions, then a frame grid of three-column argument cells in the page column, closed by a hatched gap. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'hero-with-opening', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `hero`, `hero-title`, `button`, `section-container`, `section-module`, `frame-box`, `card-grid`, `topic` and `section-gap`. The grid starts at the hero floor with no gap, so the arguments read as the second half of the hero.
useWhen: To open a product page that argues on three or six claims right under its headline.
avoidWhen: For an opening band with no arguments → use `hero-band`.
For a reasons band further down the page → use `feature-tiles` or `use-cases`.
related: hero-band` — the opening band without the argument grid.
topic` — the icon, heading and sentence each argument is rendered with.
bestPractices: Use three or six items so every row of the grid is full.
Keep each item to a short title and one sentence.
A title longer than 45 characters widens the headline column so it breaks into two lines instead of three.

props.name: title
props.doc: Page headline, rendered as the page `h1`; the band renders nothing when empty. A title longer than 45 characters widens the headline column.

props.name: primaryAction
props.doc: First button under the headline; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: Second, outlined button beside the first; `{ label, href, trailing?, target? }`. Shown only with a label and a link.

props.name: items
props.doc: The arguments in reading order, three to a row; each is `{ icon, title, description }`. The grid renders only when there are items.
